bigPicture.subtitle: Grow in Grace and Knowledge Until the Day Dawns
bigPicture.thesis: If we had to summarize the Book of 2 Peter in one overarching thought, it is this: God has given you everything you need for life and godliness, so grow diligently in the knowledge of Christ, anchor yourself in the eyewitness testimony of the apostles and the Spirit-breathed Scriptures, reject teachers who promise freedom while living in corruption, and live holy lives as you wait for the day of the Lord and the new heavens and new earth where righteousness dwells.
paragraphs: Second Peter is the last testament of an apostle who knew his death was near. He had been told by Jesus how he would die, and now the time had come to fold his tent (1:14). He did not use his last letter to talk about himself. He used it to remind, warn and strengthen the churches — to do what Jesus had told him to do: “You, when once you have turned again, establish your brothers” (Luke 22:32).

The letter faces a different threat from 1 Peter. There the danger was persecution from outside; here it is deception from inside. False teachers had arisen, clever and greedy, promising liberty while living as slaves of corruption, and mocking the promise of Christ's return. Peter answers them with three things: God's full provision for godliness (chapter 1), God's certain judgement and rescue (chapter 2), and God's patient but certain coming day (chapter 3).

Running through every chapter is one word: knowledge — not the proud ‘knowledge’ of the false teachers, but the personal, life-changing knowledge of Jesus Christ. The letter opens with grace and peace “multiplied in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord” (2 Peter 1:2), and closes with “But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ” (2 Peter 3:18). The answer to false teaching is not suspicion alone but growth.

The man who once walked on water and sank, who confessed Christ and denied Him, who slept in Gethsemane and drew a sword, ends his life as a steady shepherd. He has seen the majesty on the mountain, the cross on the hill and the empty tomb, and he faces his own death calmly, calling it an exodus. His final word is not about himself at all: “To him be the glory both now and forever. Amen” (2 Peter 3:18).

map.intro: 2 Peter is the twenty-second book of the New Testament, the third of the letters written to the whole church. It stands between 1 Peter and the letters of John, and it shares much of its second chapter with Jude.

sections.title: From Suffering to Deception
sections.body: 1 Peter prepared believers for the fiery trial of persecution; 2 Peter prepares them for the quieter danger of false teaching. Both letters close with the same call: be watchful and stand firm. In 1 Peter the devil prowls like a roaring lion (1 Peter 5:8); in 2 Peter he works through teachers with smooth words and greedy hearts. Together the two letters equip the church to stand against both the sword and the lie.

sections.title: The Apostolic Testimony and the Canon
sections.body: 2 Peter makes some of the clearest statements in the New Testament about how God speaks. The apostles were eyewitnesses, not myth-makers (1:16). The prophets spoke as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit (1:21). And Paul's letters, though sometimes hard, are placed alongside ‘the other Scriptures’ (3:16). Questions about the letter's authorship have been raised since early times, and many scholars still doubt it; this study has read it as it presents itself — the final word of the apostle Peter — and as the church received it.

sections.title: Hard Passages Read Honestly
sections.body: ‘Partakers of the divine nature’ (1:4) means sharing God's life and character, not becoming God. ‘The Master who bought them’ (2:1) is read in different ways — whether Christ's death was for those who finally perish, or whether these teachers only professed to be redeemed. Tartarus (2:4) is a Greek word Peter borrows for the prison of fallen angels. The dog and the sow (2:22) suggest that those who return to corruption were never truly changed. God's desire that none perish (3:9) is read differently in relation to His choosing. And in 3:10 the oldest manuscripts read that the earth and its works will be ‘found’ — laid bare — rather than ‘burned up’.

sections.title: Word Families in 2 Peter
sections.body: 2 Peter's key contrast is within the know family: ἐπίγνωσις, the full personal knowledge of Christ that saves (1:2–3, 8; 2:20), and γνῶσις, knowledge that grows (1:5–6; 3:18). Other contrasts include τηρέω and φυλάσσω (the wicked kept for judgement, Noah guarded for life, 2:4–5), ἰσχύς and δύναμις (2:11), γῆ and κόσμος (3:5–6), ῥῆμα and λόγος (3:2, 5), καινός, new in kind, for the new heavens and earth (3:13), and μακροθυμία, God's long temper (3:9, 15). New members joined many families, from ἐπόπτης (eyewitness) in the see family to ἔτος (years) in the time family.

roadAhead.intro: The Road Ahead: 2 Peter ended with a warning against error and a call to grow in the knowledge of Christ while waiting for His coming. The next two books are 1 John, a letter about fellowship with God, walking in the light, love for one another, and testing the spirits; and 2 John, a short letter to ‘the chosen lady’ urging believers to walk in truth and love and not to welcome deceivers.

books.connection: Like Peter, John writes as an eyewitness: “That which was from the beginning, that which we have heard, that which we have seen with our eyes, that which we saw, and our hands touched, concerning the Word of life” (1 John 1:1). Peter warned of false teachers; John says, “Beloved, don’t believe every spirit, but test the spirits, whether they are of God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world” (1 John 4:1). Peter called believers to holiness while they wait; John says, “Now, little children, remain in him, that when he appears, we may have boldness, and not be ashamed before him at his coming” (1 John 2:28). And the knowledge Peter urged them to grow in, John unfolds as fellowship: “But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ, his Son, cleanses us from all sin” (1 John 1:7). Watch for John's tests of true faith: belief in Jesus, obedience and love.

The shortest book of the New Testament carries 2 Peter's warning into the home. John writes as “The elder, to the chosen lady and her children, whom I love in truth” (2 John 1:1), and warns, “For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who don’t confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh” (2 John 1:7). Like Peter, he holds truth and love together: “This is love, that we should walk according to his commandments” (2 John 1:6). And he gives practical guidance about false teachers: “If anyone comes to you, and doesn’t bring this teaching, don’t receive him into your house, and don’t welcome him” (2 John 1:10). Watch for how John guards both love and truth.

themesMastered.title: Everything for Life and Godliness, and the Call to Grow
themesMastered.body: God's “divine power has granted to us all things that pertain to life and godliness” (2 Peter 1:3), and through His promises believers share the divine nature. So with all diligence they add to faith moral excellence, knowledge, self-control, perseverance, godliness, brotherly affection and love. These qualities keep them fruitful, confirm their calling and election, and ensure a rich welcome into the eternal kingdom.

themesMastered.title: Eyewitnesses and the Sure Word
themesMastered.body: The gospel rests on eyewitness testimony: “we were eyewitnesses of his majesty” (2 Peter 1:16). And the prophetic word is a lamp in a dark place until the day dawns, because “holy men of God spoke, being moved by the Holy Spirit” (2 Peter 1:21). The words of the prophets and the commands of the apostles, including Paul's letters, are Scripture — to be heeded, not twisted.

themesMastered.title: False Teachers Exposed
themesMastered.body: False teachers arise within the church, bringing in destructive heresies, denying the Master who bought them, exploiting believers with greed and fabricated words, and enticing the unstable with promises of freedom while they are slaves of corruption. Their judgement is certain. And “the Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment” (2 Peter 2:9).

themesMastered.title: God's Patience and the Day of the Lord
themesMastered.body: Scoffers mock the promise of Christ's coming, deliberately forgetting creation and the flood. But with the Lord a day is as a thousand years, and His apparent slowness is patience: “not wishing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance” (2 Peter 3:9). Yet the day of the Lord will come like a thief, and the heavens and earth will be dissolved and laid bare.

themesMastered.title: Holy Living While We Wait
themesMastered.body: Since everything will be dissolved, believers live “in holy living and godliness” (2 Peter 3:11), waiting for and hastening the day of God, looking for “new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells” (2 Peter 3:13). They are diligent to be found spotless and at peace, guard themselves against error, and “grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ” (2 Peter 3:18).

experientialLesson.intro: How do you walk out the Book of 2 Peter practically moving forward? Here is your experiential blueprint:

steps.title: Climb the Ladder of Growth
steps.lesson: The Lesson: “Yes, and for this very cause adding on your part all diligence, in your faith supply moral excellence; and in moral excellence, knowledge” (2 Peter 1:5).
steps.practice: The Practice: Take eight weeks to work through the eight qualities of 1:5–7, one each week. For each, read a Scripture about it, ask God to grow it in you, and choose one concrete action to practise it. At the end, thank God that His divine power has given you everything you need, and ask a trusted friend which quality they have seen grow.

steps.title: Anchor Yourself in the Word and Test Every Teacher
steps.lesson: The Lesson: “We have the more sure word of prophecy; and you do well that you heed it, as to a lamp shining in a dark place” (2 Peter 1:19).
steps.practice: The Practice: Establish a daily habit of reading Scripture before any other media. Keep a ‘discernment card’ with four questions — Does it exalt Jesus as Lord? Does it agree with Scripture? Does it lead to holiness and love? Does the teacher's life and use of money match the message? — and use it on every new teaching you hear this month.

steps.title: Live Today in the Light of That Day
steps.lesson: The Lesson: “Therefore since all these things will be destroyed like this, what kind of people ought you to be in holy living and godliness” (2 Peter 3:11).
steps.practice: The Practice: Begin each morning this month by asking, ‘If Jesus returned today, what kind of person would I want Him to find?’ Then do one specific thing that answers it. Pray daily for three people who do not yet know Christ, thanking God that His patience is giving them time, and look for an opportunity to share the hope of the new creation.

finalDeclaration: “Lord Jesus, my God and Saviour, I declare that Your divine power has given me everything I need for life and godliness. Through Your precious and very great promises I share in Your nature and have escaped the corruption of the world. I will be diligent to add to my faith virtue, knowledge, self-control, perseverance, godliness, brotherly affection and love, and I will not be idle or unfruitful in knowing You. I will not forget that You cleansed me from my old sins. I will make my calling and election sure, and I will receive a rich welcome into Your eternal kingdom. I do not follow clever myths; I trust the eyewitnesses who saw Your majesty and heard the Father's voice, and I trust the Scriptures spoken by holy men carried along by the Holy Spirit. Your word is my lamp until the day dawns and the morning star rises in my heart. I reject every teacher who denies You as Master, who exploits Your people, or who promises freedom while living in corruption. I declare that You know how to rescue the godly and to hold the unrighteous for judgement. I will not scoff at Your coming. Your delay is patience, not slowness, and You do not want anyone to perish. Your day will come like a thief, so I will live in holiness and godliness, waiting for and hastening Your coming, looking for new heavens and a new earth where righteousness dwells. I will be diligent to be found by You in peace, spotless and blameless. I will guard myself from error and keep my footing. And I will grow in Your grace and in knowing You, my Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To You be the glory, now and to the day of eternity. In the mighty name of Jesus, Amen!”
